position_title: Staff Assistant/Military & Veterans Constituent Service Representative
description: The District Office of Congresswoman Katherine M. Clark (MA-05) is accepting applicants for the position of Staff Assistant/Military & Veterans Constituent Service Representative. This position is responsible for a wide range of outreach, relationship management, event coordination, and correspondence. This is a full-time position. Office staff are currently working in person, remotely, or in a hybrid model depending on the needs of the office.
responsibilities: Acts as the representative for the Congresswoman within their area of responsibility including answering casework correspondence, meeting with constituents, verbal communications with constituents, and serving as a liaison with federal, district, and local agencies
Manages mail operations, maintains administrative files, and coordinates office supply re-orders
Hosts periodic office hours at varied locations for constituents throughout the district
Leads process for military service academy nominations, planning outreach to interested students, reviewing applications, and providing recommendations to Congresswoman
Answers constituent calls, refers cases, and assists in internship supervision

Strong written and oral communicator

description: A senior Republican member serving on the House Financial Services Committee is seeking a fellow to assist the Legislative Team in covering the committee and research portfolio. This is a paid opportunity. The person in this role will work on substantive financial services issues like banking, crypto, housing, capital markets, fintech, insurance, and monetary policy in the Member's personal office. The fellow will also be asked to assist the Legislative Director in research projects. The fellow will also be attending hearings, monitoring legislation and regulations, assisting with official and constituent correspondence, providing meeting materials, and more. The fellow should leave this role with an in-depth understanding of how Capitol Hill operates, as well as the major policy issues in financial services.

Preparing materials for hearings, markups, and the House floor
Conducting policy research
Taking notes at meetings, hearings, briefings, and other events you attend
Tracking legislation and official correspondence
Observing House proceedings
Drafting constituent correspondence
qualifications: Excellent writers
Able to work in a fast-paced environment
Good judgment

description: Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) seeks an experienced full-time Field Representative to serve as the Member's primary liaison to veterans, active-duty service members, military families, first responders, and some rural communities across the district. The Field Representative reports to the Deputy Chief of Staff and works in close coordination with the Legislative Director, Casework Team, and Communications staff. Existing relationships and experience within the military community are required. The salary range for this position is $55,000 to $65,000 annually, commensurate with experience, and includes health, vision, and dental insurance, paid vacation days and sick time, student loan repayment, and transit benefits. description: Representative Raul Ruiz, M.D. is a Senior Member of the Energy and Commerce Committee and former Chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus. Seeking interested and qualified candidates for the position of Executive Assistant and Scheduler in his Washington, D.C. office. This is not an entry-level position. Salary is commensurate with experience; the office offers competitive and comprehensive benefits. The Executive Assistant and Scheduler will manage the Congressman's schedule from DC to California and support the smooth daily operations of the office, reporting directly to the Chief of Staff. This role works closely with the Chief of Staff, District Director, Legislative Director, and Communications Director to ensure all scheduling needs are met and the Member stays on schedule throughout the day. Additionally, the Executive Assistant serves as the direct administrative assistant for the Congressman managing the Member's schedule, logistics, personal office, workflow, and information needs. We are looking for someone who thrives under pressure, takes pride in precision, and brings energy, optimism, and grit to the job every day. The ideal candidate will develop in-depth knowledge of the district and key stakeholders to meet the office's strategic goals and priorities.
responsibilities: Coordinate, maintain, and execute the Congressman's daily schedule, ensuring proper time allocation for preparation, travel, and transitions between meetings and events.
Serve as the primary entry point for constituents and stakeholders seeking to engage the office.
Perform intake and internal processing of all D.C. and district scheduling requests in a timely manner; ensure district requests are coordinated with the district team.
Track and manage RSVPs, invitations, and event logistics; ensure the Member is appropriately staffed for all meetings and events.
Anticipate and troubleshoot scheduling conflicts in real time, adjusting priorities as needed in a fast-moving environment.
Manage last-minute changes, cancellations, and urgent requests with professionalism and discretion.
Ensure briefing materials are prepared and provided for each event and meeting, and that staff receive appropriate advance notice.
Arrange all official travel for the Congressman and ensure travel logistics are properly coordinated.
Draft and manage follow-up correspondence, including thank-you letters and scheduling confirmations.
Manage Member reimbursements, office purchase card, and asset management.
Implement and maintain scheduling protocols and best practices to improve office efficiency.
Ensure compliance with all office policies, procedures, and practices.
Supervise Staff Assistant, including providing feedback and conducting performance reviews.
Perform additional duties as assigned by the Congressman and Chief of Staff.
qualifications: A bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience.
Exceptional organizational, communication, and attention-to-detail skills.
Strong multitasking abilities and follow-through; demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Demonstrated problem-solving skills and a proactive, solutions-oriented mindset.
Sound judgment and the ability to anticipate challenges before they arise.
Proficiency with video conferencing and meeting platforms and scheduling tools.
The ability to work collaboratively in a team setting while maintaining professionalism under pressure.
Willingness to work flexible hours, including long hours, nights, and weekends.
California ties are a plus.

description: Congresswoman Maxine Dexter is a physician, a founding member of the Democratic Doctors Caucus, and one of Congress's most committed voices on healthcare, climate, immigrant rights, and working families. Her office is seeking an experienced, creative, and strategic Communications Director in her Washington, D.C. office. This is a senior role with real creative authority. You will set the communications agenda, shape the Congresswoman's public voice, manage a small and talented team, and be a key thought partner to the Chief of Staff, Legislative Director, and District Director. The ability to maintain a flexible schedule, including evenings and weekends as necessary—with the ability to flex time during slower periods—is essential. Dexter's Portland-based district is highly engaged, and her communications operation needs to match that energy. This is a fun office that moves fast, takes the work seriously, and believes that good communication is itself a form of advocacy. This is not an entry-level position. description: Congressman Ro Khanna's district office in Santa Clara has an immediate opening for a Caseworker/Field Representative, which involves both casework and community outreach. This is a non-supervisory position. The starting salary is $71,000 per year. The application process may include several interviews and a practical test of relevant skills. There is one current job vacancy, and the office has the right to fill any number of positions vacant or becoming vacant during the life of postings. This position ends on November 6, 2026 with the option to extend depending on office needs and available budget. The Caseworker/Field Representative is empowered to monitor issues that impact residents, serve as a liaison to federal agencies and state/local representatives, and respond to constituent inquiries through written and oral communication. A primary duty is helping local residents resolve casework problems with federal government agencies, including US Citizenship & Immigration Services, Department of State, Veterans Affairs, Internal Revenue Service, and Social Security Administration. The position also involves representing the Congressman in a variety of community activities, including interacting with leaders of community groups and local organizations, as well as local and state elected officials and stakeholders. The duties involve special project coordination and helping the staff team manage monthly town hall meetings and special events hosted by the Congressman, such as issues-based forums and roundtable meetings. The successful candidate will also help train and mentor student interns. Residency in the district is preferred, as is a knowledge of the region. The Caseworker/Field Representative is a represented position, part of the Congressional Workers Union, and reports to the District Director and Director of Constituent Services, or their designees. Work is mainly performed in an office environment. Must have a driver's license, access to a car and the ability to drive to perform field work. The district office functions on a hybrid basis, with each staff member expected to be based in the physical office three days a week and allowed to work from home two days a week. The office is open 9:00am-5:00pm Monday-Friday, with a full lunch hour. Staff can expect to work 2-3 times per week after hours on community events. Commensurate flex time will be granted upon request. Benefits include annual leave accrual of 1.25 days per month (15 days per year), 15 annual Sick/Mental Health Days, flex time, group health insurance, retirement savings, and a potential annual bonus.
